the immunoprotetasome/proteasomes ratio increases in the hippocampus of aged rats, and that the age‐induced neuro‐inflammatory processes and the transcriptional factor Zif268 are the main responsible factors.

the age‐associated increase in the content of immunoprote asomes in hippocampus is because of neuroinflammation, and is associated with a decrease in the expression of the transcriptional repressor Zif268.

the molecular and functional aspects related to the age‐related changes of proteasomes in the hippocampus.
the study of the age‐related increase in hippocampal immunosuppression and its relationship with neuroinflammation.
the molecular and functional aspects of age‐related changes in proteasomal activity in the rat hippocampus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the age‐dependent changes in proteasome activity could, in large part, be attributed to an increased content of immunoproteases in the aged hippocampus, which in turn, would be mostly related to the neuroinflammatory processes that accompany aging.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the immunoprotasome content is increased in the hippocampus of aged rats, and that neuroinflammatory processes, associated to aging, are responsible for the increase of the immunoproteosome content in the hippocampus.
the age‐dependent increase in the immunosubunits of proteasome is a compensatory mechanism to maintain the proteasome proteolytic activity in the aged hippocampus.

age‐related changes in the proteasomal composition in hippocampus are associated to a higher content of immunoproteosomes, which may be involved in the increased hydrophobicity observed in aged hippocampus.
the age‐dependent increase in the content of immunoproteases in the hippocampus is mostly because of the neuroinflammatory processes that accompany aging.
